quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on navigating the starting lineup without Zion Williamson
quotes.excerpt: we've always talked about next man up mentality

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: Zion rest. Just rest, anything else?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: No, just rest. We've always talked about next man up mentality, and so we've have guys that have started before, that have been in lineup, that have been out of the lineup. So it's going to be that tonight and we're going to have guys that are ready to go.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley confirms Zion Williamson is out tonight for rest and emphasizes the next man up mentality for the Pelicans lineup.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley explains that Zion Williamson is resting for the upcoming game against the Warriors.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on defensive adjustments and team accountability
quotes.excerpt: we had a couple missed assignments, understanding personnel, game plan situations

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Last night after the game when you spoke about the defense, you very strongly said unacceptable. Tonight in this situation, where would you like to see that energy and the adjustments shown to you?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: Just tied together. I think that's the biggest thing. We had a couple missed assignments, understanding personnel, game plan situations, those were some things that we fell into last night. And so this is a team that's going to test that tonight, all of it. And I think our ability to stay connected in those areas, they're going to hit some halacious shots and that's what they do and you're not going to try to deny that. But we cannot react to that. We have to stick to our game plan and know what we're willing to take away, but also what we're willing to give up.

quotes.social_post: After calling the defense unacceptable last night Jamahl Mosley says the key tonight is staying connected and sticking to the game plan regardless of the shots the opponent makes.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses the need for defensive connectivity and sticking to the game plan following a poor defensive performance.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the sustained high-level play of Steph, Draymond, and Al Horford
quotes.excerpt: they understand exactly what it takes to win in this league

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Can you explain how Steph and Draymon and Al Horford are playing still at such a high level at their age?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: It goes back to the question somebody asked me weeks ago about LeBron. Their ability to take care of their body, their professionalism, their work ethic, their care factor for the game. They understand exactly what it takes to win in this league, but also know how to sustain themselves in this league. And I think that's what they do, the work ethic in the off season, making sure they're taking their care of their bodies, their recovery, the rest, those are all the key pieces. And then the last part of it is the basketball IQ. You can play a long time if you understand the game and how to get open, how to create for your teammates.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley credits the sustained high level play of veterans like Steph Curry and Draymond Green to their professionalism work ethic and high basketball IQ.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the factors that allow veteran players like Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, and Al Horford to maintain high-level play.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the challenge of defending Steph Curry
quotes.excerpt: anywhere he steps on the court is a challenge

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Is trying to stay with Steph off the ball one of the biggest challenges defensively that you're going to have tonight?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: Anywhere he steps on the court is a challenge. And I think because of his range, because of his movement, because of his IQ, because now even at the highest level, him getting to the foul line on top of not just knocking threes down, has changed the game even more so for what he's done. But again, that goes back to the IQ that if he doesn't have to run around as much, now he's finding ways to get baited into getting fouls and getting to the free throw line. So that's what he's done in order to expand and keep growing his game even in this year.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the challenge of defending Steph Curry saying anywhere he steps on the court is a challenge because of his range movement and ability to get to the free throw line.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley describes the defensive challenges posed by Stephen Curry's movement, range, and ability to draw fouls.
